title: Log smooth and log etale morphisms of fs log schemes
statement: Let $f:(V,M_V)\to(B,M_B)$ be a morphism of locally Noetherian fs log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. For a commutative monoid $P$, write $\mathbf Z[P]=\bigoplus_{p\in P}\mathbf Zz^p$ with $z^pz^q=z^{p+q}$. The morphism is log smooth if etale locally on source and target there are compatible fine saturated charts $P\to M_B$, $Q\to M_V$ and $u:P\to Q$ such that the kernel and the torsion subgroup of the cokernel of $u^{\rm gp}$ are finite of orders invertible on $V$, and the comparison morphism $V\to B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. It is log etale if charts can be chosen with both the kernel and the whole cokernel finite of invertible orders and the comparison morphism etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Charts and group completions mean those of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]; the comparisons use scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2 and its proof, pp.136--138, chart criterion recalled there; Expose XVI 3.6.1--3.6.3, p.252 (trait version). General criterion is Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine--Illusie, Theorem 3.5 (WANTED locally).

from.place: Proof Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality, regular finite-torsion local model; pointwise purity and composition used to compare the normalized curve with the ambient regular scheme. Input: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair. More precisely: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph. Specifically: The fs charts used in XVI 3.7 for the semistable model, tame trait change and log resolution.
